name: read_bcf
signature: read_bcf(path, region := NULL, index_path := NULL, tidy_format := FALSE, additional_csq_column_types := NULL)
description: Read VCF and BCF variant data with typed INFO, FORMAT, typed CSQ/ANN/BCSQ subfields, optional tidy sample output, and optional bcftools-style CSQ type overrides.
examples: SELECT CHROM, POS, REF, ALT FROM read_bcf('vcf_file.bcf') LIMIT 5;

name: read_bam
signature: read_bam(path, standard_tags := FALSE, auxiliary_tags := FALSE, region := NULL, index_path := NULL, reference := NULL, sequence_encoding := 'string', quality_representation := 'string')
description: Read SAM, BAM, and CRAM alignments with optional typed SAMtags and auxiliary tag maps. Use sequence_encoding := 'nt16' to return SEQ as UTINYINT[] and quality_representation := 'phred' to return QUAL as UTINYINT[] instead of VARCHAR.
examples: SELECT QNAME, FLAG, RNAME, POS FROM read_bam('range.bam') LIMIT 5;

name: read_fasta
signature: read_fasta(path, region := NULL, index_path := NULL, sequence_encoding := 'string')
description: Read FASTA records or indexed FASTA regions as sequence rows. Use sequence_encoding := 'nt16' to return SEQUENCE as UTINYINT[] (htslib nt16 4-bit codes) instead of VARCHAR.

name: read_bed
description: Read BED3-BED12 interval files with canonical typed columns and optional tabix-backed region filtering.
examples: SELECT chrom, start, "end", name FROM read_bed('targets.bed') LIMIT 5;

name: fasta_nuc
signature: fasta_nuc(path, bed_path := NULL, bin_width := NULL, region := NULL, index_path := NULL, bed_index_path := NULL, include_seq := FALSE)
description: Compute bedtools nuc-style nucleotide composition for supplied BED intervals or generated fixed-width bins over a FASTA reference.
examples: SELECT chrom, start, "end", pct_gc FROM fasta_nuc('ce.fa', bin_width := 1000) LIMIT 5;

name: read_fastq
signature: read_fastq(path, interleaved := FALSE, mate_path := NULL, sequence_encoding := 'string', quality_representation := 'string', input_quality_encoding := 'phred33')
description: Read single-end, paired-end, or interleaved FASTQ files with optional legacy quality decoding. By default, FASTQ qualities are interpreted as modern Phred+33 input. Use sequence_encoding := 'nt16' to return SEQUENCE as UTINYINT[] and quality_representation := 'phred' to return QUALITY as UTINYINT[] instead of VARCHAR. input_quality_encoding accepts 'phred33', 'auto', 'phred64', or 'solexa64'.
examples: SELECT NAME, MATE FROM read_fastq('r1.fq', mate_path := 'r2.fq') LIMIT 5;

name: detect_quality_encoding
description: Inspect a FASTQ file's observed quality ASCII range and report compatible legacy encodings with a heuristic guessed encoding.

name: read_gff
signature: read_gff(path, header_names := NULL, header := FALSE, column_types := NULL, auto_detect := FALSE, attributes_map := FALSE, region := NULL, index_path := NULL)
description: Read GFF annotations with optional parsed attribute maps and indexed region filtering.
examples: SELECT seqname, feature, start, "end" FROM read_gff('gff_file.gff.gz') LIMIT 5;

name: read_gtf
signature: read_gtf(path, header_names := NULL, header := FALSE, column_types := NULL, auto_detect := FALSE, attributes_map := FALSE, region := NULL, index_path := NULL)
description: Read GTF annotations with optional parsed attribute maps and indexed region filtering.
examples: SELECT seqname, feature, start, "end" FROM read_gtf('annotations.gtf.gz') LIMIT 5;

name: read_tabix
signature: read_tabix(path, header_names := NULL, header := FALSE, column_types := NULL, auto_detect := FALSE, region := NULL, index_path := NULL)
description: Read generic tabix-indexed text data with optional header handling and type inference.

name: fasta_index
description: Build a FASTA index (.fai) and return a single row with columns success (BOOLEAN) and index_path (VARCHAR).

name: bgzip
signature: bgzip(path, output_path := NULL, threads := 4, level := -1, keep := TRUE, overwrite := FALSE)
description: Compress a plain file to BGZF and return the created output path and byte counts.

name: bgunzip
signature: bgunzip(path, output_path := NULL, threads := 4, keep := TRUE, overwrite := FALSE)
description: Decompress a BGZF-compressed file and return the created output path and byte counts.

name: bam_index
description: Build a BAM or CRAM index and report the written index path and format.

name: bcf_index
signature: bcf_index(path, index_path := NULL, min_shift := NULL, threads := 4)
description: Build a TBI or CSI index for a VCF or BCF file and report the written index path and format.

name: tabix_index
signature: tabix_index(path, preset := 'vcf', index_path := NULL, min_shift := 0, threads := 4, seq_col := NULL, start_col := NULL, end_col := NULL, comment_char := NULL, skip_lines := NULL)
description: Build a tabix index for a BGZF-compressed text file using a preset or explicit coordinate columns.

name: read_hts_header
description: Inspect HTS headers in parsed, raw, or combined form across supported formats.
examples: SELECT record_type, id FROM read_hts_header('formatcols.vcf.gz') LIMIT 10;

name: read_hts_index
description: Inspect high-level HTS index metadata such as sequence names and mapped counts.

name: read_hts_index_spans
description: Expand index metadata into span and chunk rows suitable for low-level index inspection.
examples: SELECT seqname, chunk_beg_vo, chunk_end_vo FROM read_hts_index_spans('vcf_file.bcf') LIMIT 5;

name: read_hts_index_raw
description: Return the raw on-disk HTS index blob together with basic identifying metadata.

name: bcftools_liftover
signature: bcftools_liftover(chrom, pos, ref, alt, chain_path, dst_fasta_ref, src_fasta_ref, max_snp_gap, max_indel_inc, lift_mt, end_pos, no_left_align)
description: Row-oriented liftover kernel intended to mirror bcftools +liftover semantics as closely as possible while returning one STRUCT per input row with fields: src_chrom, src_pos, src_ref, src_alt, dest_chrom, dest_pos, dest_end, dest_ref, dest_alt, mapped, reverse_complemented, swap, reject_reason, and note. Set no_left_align := true to skip post-liftover left-alignment of lifted indels (mirrors --no-left-align in bcftools +liftover).
examples: SELECT (bcftools_liftover(chrom, pos, ref, alt, 'hg19ToHg38.over.chain.gz', 'hg38.fa', 'hg19.fa', 1, 250, false, NULL::BIGINT, false)).dest_pos FROM variants;

name: duckdb_liftover
signature: duckdb_liftover(table_name, chrom_col, pos_col, ref_col := NULL, alt_col := NULL, chain_path := NULL, dst_fasta_ref := NULL, src_fasta_ref := NULL, max_snp_gap := 1, max_indel_inc := 250, lift_mt := false, end_pos_col := NULL, no_left_align := false)
description: DuckDB-specific wrapper over bcftools_liftover that takes either a table name or a derived-table expression plus column-name strings for chrom/pos/ref/alt and returns the lifted table. The no_left_align parameter mirrors --no-left-align in bcftools +liftover.
examples: SELECT * FROM duckdb_liftover('variants', 'chrom', 'pos', ref_col := 'ref', alt_col := 'alt', chain_path := 'hg19ToHg38.over.chain.gz', dst_fasta_ref := 'hg38.fa'); || SELECT * FROM duckdb_liftover('(SELECT chrom, pos, ref, alt FROM variants) AS v', 'chrom', 'pos', ref_col := 'ref', alt_col := 'alt', chain_path := 'hg19ToHg38.over.chain.gz', dst_fasta_ref := 'hg38.fa');

name: bcftools_score
signature: bcftools_score(bcf_path, summary_path, use := NULL, columns := 'PLINK', columns_file := NULL, q_score_thr := NULL, use_variant_id := FALSE, counts := FALSE, samples := NULL, force_samples := FALSE, regions := NULL, regions_file := NULL, regions_overlap := 1, targets := NULL, targets_file := NULL, targets_overlap := 0, apply_filters := NULL, include := NULL, exclude := NULL)
description: Compute polygenic scores from one genotype BCF/VCF and one summary-statistics file with bcftools +score-compatible GT/DS/HDS/AP/GP/AS dosage semantics, sample subsetting, and region/target/FILTER-string controls.

name: bcftools_munge_row
signature: bcftools_munge_row(chrom, pos, a1, a2, id, p, z, or, beta, n, n_cas, n_con, info, frq, se, lp, ac, neff, neffdiv2, het_i2, het_p, het_lp, dire, fasta_ref, iffy_tag := 'IFFY', mismatch_tag := 'REF_MISMATCH', ns := NULL, nc := NULL, ne := NULL)
description: Normalize one summary-statistics row into GWAS-VCF-style fields (chrom/pos/ref/alt/effect metrics), resolving REF/ALT orientation against a FASTA reference and applying swap-aware sign/frequency/count transforms. The output flag `alleles_swapped` means REF/ALT orientation was swapped to match the FASTA reference.
examples: SELECT (bcftools_munge_row('chr1', 12345, 'A', 'G', 'rs1', 0.01, NULL, NULL, 0.12, 1000, NULL, NULL, NULL, 0.3, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, 'ref.fa')).ref;

name: duckdb_munge
signature: duckdb_munge(table_name, preset := '', column_map := map([''], ['']), column_map_file := '', fasta_ref := NULL, iffy_tag := 'IFFY', mismatch_tag := 'REF_MISMATCH', ns := NULL, nc := NULL, ne := NULL)
description: DuckDB macro wrapper over bcftools_munge_row that maps source columns (via preset or explicit map) and returns normalized GWAS-VCF-style rows with lean outputs and explicit `alleles_swapped` semantics. Output columns: chrom, pos, id, ref, alt, alleles_swapped, filter, ns, ez, nc, es, se, lp, af, ac, ne (16 columns). For METAL meta-analysis output with SI/I2/CQ/ED columns, use duckdb_munge_metal.
examples: SELECT * FROM duckdb_munge('gwas_table', preset := 'PLINK', fasta_ref := 'ref.fa'); || SELECT * FROM duckdb_munge('(SELECT * FROM gwas_table) AS s', column_map := map(['CHR','BP','A1','A2','SNP'], ['chrom','pos','ea','nea','id']), fasta_ref := 'ref.fa');

name: duckdb_munge_metal
signature: duckdb_munge_metal(table_name, preset := '', column_map := map([''], ['']), column_map_file := '', fasta_ref := NULL, iffy_tag := 'IFFY', mismatch_tag := 'REF_MISMATCH', ns := NULL, nc := NULL, ne := NULL)
description: Extended munge macro with METAL meta-analysis output columns. Same as duckdb_munge but additionally emits: si (imputation info, from INFO input), i2 (Cochran's I² heterogeneity, from HET_I2), cq (Cochran's Q -log10 p, from HET_LP or -log10(HET_P)), and ed (effect direction string, from DIRE; +/- flipped on allele swap). The R wrapper rduckhts_munge() auto-dispatches to this macro when metal keys (INFO, HET_I2, HET_P, HET_LP, DIRE) are present in the resolved column map.
examples: SELECT * FROM duckdb_munge_metal('metal_results', preset := 'METAL', fasta_ref := 'ref.fa'); || SELECT * FROM duckdb_munge_metal('meta', column_map := map(['CHR','BP','A1','A2','SNP','HET_I2','DIRE'], ['chr','pos','ea','nea','snp','HetISq','Direction']), fasta_ref := 'ref.fa');

name: seq_revcomp
description: Compute the reverse complement of a DNA sequence using A, C, G, T, and N bases.

name: seq_canonical
description: Return the lexicographically smaller of a sequence and its reverse complement.

name: seq_hash_2bit
description: Encode a short DNA sequence as a 2-bit unsigned integer hash.

name: seq_encode_4bit
description: Encode an IUPAC DNA sequence as a list of 4-bit base codes, preserving ambiguity symbols including N.

name: seq_decode_4bit
description: Decode a list of 4-bit IUPAC DNA base codes back into a sequence string.

name: seq_gc_content
description: Compute GC fraction for a DNA sequence as a value between 0 and 1.

name: seq_kmers
description: Expand a sequence into positional k-mers with optional canonicalization.

name: sam_flag_bits
description: Decode a SAM flag into a struct of boolean bit fields using explicit SAM-oriented names such as `is_paired`, `is_proper_pair`, `is_next_segment_unmapped`, and `is_supplementary`.

name: sam_flag_has
description: Test whether any bits from the provided SAM flag mask are set in a flag value.

name: is_forward_aligned
description: Test whether a mapped segment is aligned to the forward strand. Returns `NULL` for unmapped segments because SAM flag `0x10` does not define genomic strand when `0x4` is set.

name: cigar_has_soft_clip
description: Test whether a CIGAR string contains any soft-clipped segment (`S`).

name: cigar_has_hard_clip
description: Test whether a CIGAR string contains any hard-clipped segment (`H`).

name: cigar_left_soft_clip
description: Return the left-end soft-clipped length from a CIGAR string, or zero if the alignment does not start with `S`.

name: cigar_right_soft_clip
description: Return the right-end soft-clipped length from a CIGAR string, or zero if the alignment does not end with `S`.

name: cigar_query_length
description: Return the query-consuming length from a CIGAR string, counting `M`, `I`, `S`, `=`, and `X`.

name: cigar_aligned_query_length
description: Return the aligned query length from a CIGAR string, counting `M`, `=`, and `X` but excluding clips and insertions.

name: cigar_reference_length
description: Return the reference-consuming length from a CIGAR string, counting `M`, `D`, `N`, `=`, and `X`.

name: cigar_has_op
description: Test whether a CIGAR string contains at least one instance of the requested operator.

name: is_paired
description: Test whether the SAM flag indicates that the template has multiple segments in sequencing (`0x1`).

name: is_proper_pair
description: Test whether the SAM flag indicates that each segment is properly aligned according to the aligner (`0x2`).

name: is_unmapped
description: Test whether the read itself is unmapped according to the SAM flag.

name: is_next_segment_unmapped
description: Test whether the next segment in the template is flagged as unmapped (`0x8`).

name: is_reverse_complemented
description: Test whether `SEQ` is stored reverse complemented (`0x10`); for mapped reads this corresponds to reverse-strand alignment.

name: is_next_segment_reverse_complemented
description: Test whether `SEQ` of the next segment in the template is stored reverse complemented (`0x20`).

name: is_first_segment
description: Test whether the read is marked as the first segment in the template.

name: is_last_segment
description: Test whether the read is marked as the last segment in the template.

name: is_secondary
description: Test whether the alignment is marked as secondary.

name: is_qc_fail
description: Test whether the read failed vendor or pipeline quality checks.

name: is_duplicate
description: Test whether the alignment is flagged as a duplicate.

name: is_supplementary
description: Test whether the alignment is marked as supplementary.
